provenance.row: B4 control 1 of 2 - the first phantom-release direction
provenance.subject: lagging member ABSENT at M must produce recovery at M with NO patch
provenance.design_reference: docs/aben-design.md section 9, B4 control pair, and section 3's mutation controls: 'lagging-member-absent-at-M must produce recovery at M with no patch'

expected.group_decision: candidate is M; NO next-patch mint
expected.why: step 3 of the shared-candidate algorithm: if every moving/lagging member can publish or recover AT M and every complete member is exact at M, the candidate is M. Minting a patch here would be the bug - it would burn a version number because one member lagged, which is the phantom-release direction this control pins.

construction.warning: This is a counterfactual world and the inversion of reality is deliberate: in the real 0.7.15 cycle pypi aweb 1.27.2 was ABSENT and ghcr a2a-gateway 1.27.2 was PRESENT (see b5-false-publication-status.json). This control asserts the OPPOSITE occupancy in order to exercise the lagging-absent direction. Nothing in this file was ever true and it must never be cited as a recorded registry state.
construction.anchor_reuse_note: the SHAs are real commits (server-v1.27.1 and the 0.7.15 card SHA, both re-observed 2026-08-14) used as plausible identities so the fixture exercises identity comparison rather than degenerate placeholder strings. Their reuse here carries no claim that those commits ever produced these artifacts.

provenance.discriminates_against: b4-impossible-pre-registered-shape.control-lagging-conflicting.json, which differs ONLY in whether the lagging member's occupancy at M conflicts, and must produce a shared next patch instead of recovery. If both controls yield the same group decision, the algorithm is not reading the evidence fork and both greens are empty.
